title: Make every train structurally valid

facts.note: Train definition files and registry entries are identifiable by file kind/location in the plan tree; any such file in scope activates the rule regardless of which field changed.
Task text mentions authoring, editing, reviewing or validating trains. Term match alone does not prove train-authoring intent; file_kind is the primary signal.

values: existing train in scope for validation
facts.note: Optional diff-level signal; the rule is an unconditional invariant, so an existing invalid train in scope fires even with no relevant-field diff.

fires: Planner creates a new train definition or registry entry.
Planner edits any field of an existing train (id, category, spec path, participants, dependencies, sequence, themes, or prose) while the train is in scope.
Planner reviews or validates existing trains in the plan, even without changing them.
doesNotFire: Edits to wagons, WMBTs or acceptances when no train definition or registry entry is in scope.
Code or test changes unrelated to plan artifacts.

given: A train definition or registry entry is in scope for the plan (new or existing).
when: The planner authors, edits, reviews or validates that train, whatever field is touched.
then: The train passes all seven structural validation rules: typed train_id, category as a declared field, spec file exists, participants declared, valid dependencies, domain:resource sequence artifacts, themes declared.
prefer: Declare category in its own field with one of nominal|error|alternate|exception.
Make sure the spec file exists at the train's declared path (create it or fix the path).
List every participant the train uses in its participants list.
Point every dependency at an existing, valid train_id.
Name every artifact in the sequence as domain:resource.
Declare every theme the train uses in its themes array.
avoid: Untyped or free-form train ids that do not match train:{subject}:{slug}.
Encoding the category as a digit inside the train identity.
Declaring a spec path that has no file behind it.
Using participants, themes or dependencies that are not declared / do not resolve.
Sequence artifacts not in domain:resource form.
Treating any of the seven checks as optional or advisory.
why: Trains are consumed mechanically by the registry and validators; a train that breaks any structural rule cannot be addressed, resolved or checked reliably.
evidence: No digit-encoded category in the identity; category field present with value in {nominal, error, alternate, exception}.
Spec file exists at the declared path.
Every participant referenced is in the participants list.
Every dependency resolves to a valid train_id.
Every theme used is declared in the themes array.
verifier_detail: Source statement: a train must satisfy the documented validation rules (typed id, declared themes, spec file exists, participants declared, valid dependencies, domain:resource artifacts, category declared as a field). Term validation_rule = 'a train structural validation rule.' Seven checks: (1) train_id matches train:{subject}:{slug}; (2) category is a declared field (nominal|error|alternate|exception), never a digit in the identity; (3) spec file must exist at the train's declared path; (4) all participants must be declared in participants list; (5) dependencies must reference valid train_ids; (6) artifacts in sequence must follow domain:resource pattern; (7) themes must be declared in the themes array. A train fails if any one check fails.
Spec-file existence check relies on planner.train.registry (requires edge: validation enforces spec-file existence).
Applies to every in-scope train, including existing unchanged trains; not gated on a field-level diff.

additions.text: No split: the seven checks are kept together as one obligation ('the train is structurally valid'), with each check stated as a coder-facing prefer/avoid item so none is lost for the planner. Optional future splits (category-field, spec-file-exists, participants-declared, valid-dependencies, sequence-artifact-naming, themes-declared) could be made only if each is delivered as an active convention.
